context_heading: What to understand about tax investigation advice
context: Tax investigation specialists represent you in HMRC enquiries, compliance checks and Code of Practice investigations. They manage communication with HMRC, help you understand what is being asked and work to resolve the matter. It is important not to ignore letters about a Code of Practice investigation, as doing so can make things worse.

Tax adviser is not a protected title in the UK. The Chartered Institute of Taxation (CTA qualification) and the Association of Taxation Technicians (ATT) are the main specialist bodies, and many accountants and solicitors also advise on tax. Members of these bodies follow Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation, a shared code covering honesty, confidentiality and dealing with HMRC. Tax advisers who provide services for a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and HMRC has been tightening standards for paid tax agents, so it is reasonable to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention the exact type of HMRC contact you have received, such as a compliance check letter, a Code of Practice notice, or a specific enquiry.
Say where you are based and how far you are willing to travel, since you searched for an advisor near you.
Explain whether you are an individual, a company director, or self-employed, as this affects the kind of specialist you need.
Note any deadlines or dates mentioned in HMRC correspondence so the advisor can prioritise.
Mention if you already have fee protection insurance or are unsure whether your existing policy covers investigation fees.
Share any particular concerns you have, such as worry about penalties, public naming, or the cost of representation.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the tax investigation professional
questions: What experience do you have with HMRC enquiries and Code of Practice investigations?
Are you a member of the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, or otherwise qualified in tax?
How will you communicate with HMRC on my behalf, and how often will you update me?
What are your fees, and how will you charge for the work?
Can you help me check whether my fee protection insurance covers your fees?
What is your approach to resolving the investigation, and what outcomes are realistic?

faqs.q: What should I do if I receive a letter about a Code of Practice investigation?
faqs.a: Do not ignore it. A Code of Practice investigation is serious, and you should seek specialist advice promptly. A tax investigation advisor can explain what the Code means and help you respond appropriately.

faqs.q: Will my fee protection insurance cover the cost of a tax investigation advisor?
faqs.a: Fee protection insurance may cover the costs of professional representation in an HMRC investigation, but cover varies. Check your policy or ask the advisor to help you understand it before you incur fees.

faqs.q: How do I check that a tax investigation advisor is properly qualified?
faqs.a: Tax adviser is not a protected title, so ask about qualifications such as CTA or ATT, membership of a professional body, and whether they are supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes. It is also reasonable to ask about professional indemnity insurance.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a specific tax investigation advisor near me?
faqs.a: iComply introduces you to a suitable UK tax investigation specialist based on your needs, but we do not recommend or endorse any particular professional. You decide whether to proceed after speaking with them and receiving a quote.
